title: Lessons from the States, Book VI, Ode 1: The Shû Lî
note:
Stanza 1 only, as Legge gives it.

An officer describes his melancholy and reflections on seeing the desolation of the old capital of Kâu, making his moan to Heaven because of it.

There is no specific mention of the old capital of Kâu in the piece, but the schools of Mâo and Kû are agreed in this interpretation, which is much more likely than any of the others that have been proposed.

verses.t:
There was the millet with its drooping heads;
There was the sacrificial millet coming into blade.
Slowly I moved about,
In my heart all-agitated.
Those who knew me
Said I was sad at heart.
Those who did not know me,
Said I was seeking for something.
O thou distant and azure Heaven!
By what man was this (brought about)?
